name: Steinach am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Historic market town at the Brenner Pass – once a vital trading post featuring the medieval customs house and the parish church.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Steinach am Brenner is situated in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land at an elevation of 1,048 metres above sea level in the heart of the Wipptal valley, at the confluence of the Sill and Gschnitzbach rivers. Located roughly twenty kilometres south of Innsbruck and merely twelve kilometres north of the Brenner Pass on the Italian border, this historic market town of around 3,700 inhabitants serves as the commercial, educational, and tourism hub of the entire Wipptal region. Flanked by the summits of the Stubai and Tux Alps, Steinach blends rich merchant and postal coaching heritage, advanced leisure infrastructure at the Bergeralm arena, and cutting-edge engineering associated with the Brenner Base Tunnel. As the central transport nexus, the town also provides direct access to the five untouched side valleys: Gschnitztal, Schmirntal, Valsertal, Navistal, and Obernbergtal.

Geschichte

Steinach's first recorded documentation dates to 1242 in a notarial act from Bolzano referencing an estate 'ad Stainach'; the name stems from the abundant boulders and stones lining the riverbeds of the Gschnitzbach and Sill. In 1349, the regional district court of the Wipptal was transferred here. Following the establishment of the imperial postal network under Emperor Maximilian I in 1490, Steinach evolved into the primary postal staging post and horse relay station along the vital Brenner trade artery. Emperors, Pope Pius VI, Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, and Tyrolean freedom fighter Andreas Hofer all lodged at its famed coaching inns. In 1853, a catastrophic town fire devastated the historic core. Between 1853 and 1855, architect Josef Vonstadl erected the monumental parish church of Saint Erasmus: with its imposing twin-tower facade and light-filled interior, it ranks among Tyrol's grandest Neo-Romanesque churches. Steinach was officially elevated to a market town in 1936.

Anreise

Steinach am Brenner boasts exceptional transport connectivity: by car, exit the Brenner motorway A13 directly at Steinach am Brenner (Exit 19) or Matrei/Steinach. Alternatively, the toll-free Brenner federal road B182 runs from Innsbruck through Schönberg and Matrei directly through the town centre towards the Brenner Pass. For rail travellers, Steinach am Brenner railway station is an outstanding hub: S-Bahn Tirol trains (lines S3 and S4) operate every half-hour from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof with a travel time of just 20 to 25 minutes, continuing to Brenner/Brennero with connections into South Tyrol. The station forecourt serves as the main bus terminal connecting all side valleys (VVT routes 4141 to Gschnitz, 4143 to Navis, 4144 to Schmirn/Vals, and 4145 to Obernberg).

Tipps

During the winter season, the Bergeralm ski and leisure arena right on the edge of town takes centre stage, featuring around 30 kilometres of immaculate ski runs ascending to 2,200 metres. Renowned as one of Europe's premier night-skiing destinations, the Bergeralm offers more than nine kilometres of floodlit pistes and a lit five-kilometre toboggan run. In summer, the mid-station hosts the 'Bärenbachl' water and nature adventure park, complete with interactive forest discovery trails, a wooden raft pond, and water playgrounds for children. Situated right across from the Bergeralm valley station, the BBT-Tunnelwelten exhibition centre offers free admission across 800 square metres of exhibits, showcasing a walk-in tunnel, full-scale tunnel boring machine cutterhead, train driving simulator, and interactive displays detailing the Brenner Base Tunnel. Culturally inclined visitors should not miss the monumental Erasmus church with its iconic twin towers.
